([[New Hampton, New Hampshire]]) | college = *[[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]] (2020–2023) *[[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] |highlights = *Third-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2025) *Third-team All-[[Coastal Athletic Association|CAA]] (2023) *CAA Sixth Man of the Year (2021) *CAA All-Freshman team (2021) }} '''Jahmyl Telfort''' (born April 30, 2001) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern Huskies]] and [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler Bulldogs]]. ==College career== Telfort began his collegiate career at [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]] and averaged 12.6 points per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |title=Telfort and Doherty Collect CAA Preseason Accolades |url=https://nuhuskies.com/news/2022/10/19/mens-basketball-telfort-and-doherty-collect-caa-preseason-accolades |website=[[Northeastern Huskies]] |access-date=December 9, 2025 |date=October 19, 2022}} He averaged 16.3 points and 4.5 rebounds per game as a junior, earning Third Team All-[[Coastal Athletic Association|CAA]] honors. Following the season he opted to transfer to [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{cite news |last1=Horner |first1=Scott |title=Butler basketball gets commitment from Northeastern's Jahmyl Telfort |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2023/04/13/butler-basketball-gets-commitment-from-northeasterns-jahmyl-telfort/70113487007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=true&gca-epti=z113824d00----v113824d--43--b--43--&gca-ft=195&gca-ds=sophi |access-date=December 9, 2025 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=April 13, 2023}} As a senior, Telfort averaged 13.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game, helping Butler reach the NIT. Following the season, he declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] before withdrawing and returning to school.{{cite news |last1=Horner |first1=Scott |title=Butler basketball keeps key player as Jahmyl Telfort withdraws from NBA draft |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2024/05/29/jahmyl-telfort-returns-to-butler-bulldogs-basketball-withdraws-from-nba-draft-2024-25-roster/73892160007/ |access-date=December 9, 2025 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=May 29, 2024}} In his final season, Telfort averaged 16 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.4 assists and one steal per game.{{cite news |last1=Rose |first1=Aaron |title=Toronto Raptors Take Closer Look at Canadian Wing Jahmyl Telfort Before Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/onsi/toronto-raptors-work-out-jahmyl-telfort-ahead-of-nba-draft |access-date=December 9, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 11, 2025}} He was named to the Third Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]].{{cite web |last1=Dedman |first1=John |title=Jahmyl Telfort Earns All-BIG EAST Third Team Recognition |url=https://butlersports.com/news/2025/3/9/mens-basketball-jahmyl-telfort-earns-all-big-east-third-team-recognition.aspx |website=[[Butler Bulldogs]] |access-date=December 9, 2025 |date=March 9, 2025}} ==Professional career== Undrafted after the close of his college career, Telfort signed a contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on June 27, 2025.{{cite news |last1=Rowe |first1=Daniel |title=Montreal North baller heading for the NBA |url=https://www.tsn.ca/radio/montreal-690/this-is-the-latest-montreal-baller-heading-to-the-nba-1.2328170 |access-date=27 June 2025 |work=TSN |date=27 June 2025}} On October 18, the Clippers converted Telfort's contract into a [[two-way contract]].{{Cite web|title=Clippers sign recent Butler standout Jahmyl Telfort to two-way contract|url=https://thebutlercollegian.com/2025/10/clippers-sign-recent-butler-standout-jahmyl-telfort-to-two-way-contract/|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=thebutlercollegian.com|language=en}} In six games with the [[San Diego Clippers]], he averaged 12.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game; in eight games for Los Angeles, he logged averages of 0.1 points, 0.4 rebounds, and 0.1 assists. Telfort was waived by the Clippers following the signing of [[RayJ Dennis]] on December 5.{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2025 |title=RayJ Dennis Returns to Clippers Organization, Signs Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/rayj-dennis-returns-to-clippers-organization-signs-two-way-contract/n-6306226 |url-status=live |access-date=December 9, 2025 |publisher=OurSports Central |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
